model.title: A bill to provide for the transfer of administrative jurisdiction over certain Federal land in the State of California, and for other purposes.
model.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee · Sen. Alex Padilla (D-CA)

summary.text: The bill would transfer administrative control of about 160 acres of National Forest System land in California to the Secretary of the Interior, so it would be managed as part of Yosemite National Park. It would also transfer about 170 acres of National Park System land to the Secretary of Agriculture, so it would be managed as part of Stanislaus National Forest. The two Secretaries could make minor agreed corrections and boundary adjustments to the transferred land, with those changes taking effect once published in the Federal Register. The agencies would identify and notify each other of any known hazardous substance sites, and each would remain responsible for cleanup on the land it held before the transfer. Existing rights and authorizations such as leases and permits would not be affected, though the receiving agency would take over administering them.
